SEBI Proposes Wider Foreign Investor Access to Commodity Derivatives

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed to allow foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to trade in non-agricultural commodity derivatives. This move aims to deepen the Indian commodity derivatives market. SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated that the regulator has not observed any manipulation in the newly introduced closing auction session, which is designed to align with global standards for establishing closing stock prices. Additionally, SEBI has lowered the stress testing limit for commodity derivatives.
